name: Athens
tagline: The ancient cradle of democracy beneath the Acropolis.
bestMonths: Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Sep, Oct and Nov
whenBlurb: April to June and September into October bring warm, clear days, ancient-theatre nights and Orthodox Easter's drama; skip a half-empty, oppressive July-August when the city decamps to the islands.

ourTake.lede: Athens is a summer-evening city, not a midday one. Do the Acropolis at opening or in the last hour before close, then spend the heat of the day indoors at the Acropolis Museum and the National Archaeological Museum, and let the city come alive after dark in Koukaki and Pangrati. Most people give Athens a rushed day and run for the islands; two unhurried nights and a rooftop with a Parthenon view will change their mind.
ourTake.comeIf: You want to walk through the birthplace of Western civilisation, then eat and drink well in a city that has quietly become one of Europe's most exciting.
ourTake.skipIf: You are chasing beaches or resort calm, Athens is a dense, layered city, best paired with the islands for that.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Hotel Grande Bretagne, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.description: Athens' grand address since 1874, a neo-classical landmark on Syntagma with the definitive Acropolis view from its rooftop, host to royalty and heads of state for 150 years.

items.name: King George, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.description: The discreet, jewel-box palace beside its sister Grande Bretagne, smaller, more private, with a legendary Penthouse Suite and its own private pool facing the Acropolis.

items.name: Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens
credentials: MICHELIN Guide, Three Keys (2025), the only Three-Key hotel in Athens
items.description: The Riviera icon, a pine-covered peninsula on the Saronic Gulf with three private beaches, half an hour from the centre, and the city's most complete resort experience.

items.name: One&Only Aesthesis
items.description: One&Only's first European resort, a mid-century Riviera revival on a preserved seafront in Glyfada, with airy bungalows and villas, a private beach and a Guerlain spa.

items.name: The Dolli at Acropolis
items.description: A restored neo-classical mansion on Mitropoleos, between old-town Plaka and Monastiraki, with a rooftop pool set against an unobstructed Parthenon.

items.name: Xenodocheio Milos
items.description: The hotel from the family behind the Estiatorio Milos restaurant empire, a refined, food-forward house on the elegant Vasilissis Sofias avenue near the Benaki and Cycladic museums.

items.name: Electra Metropolis Athens
credentials: Electra Hotels & Resorts, Greek luxury group
items.description: A polished, well-run city hotel in a Karantinos-designed modernist building, minutes from Syntagma, best known for its 10th-floor rooftop pool and M Bar with sweeping Acropolis views.

items.name: Ergon House Athens
items.description: A food-and-design hotel built around a working Greek agora, market, deli and restaurant on the ground floor, warm modern rooms above, in the heart of the centre.

items.name: Perianth Hotel
items.description: A contemporary art-and-design hotel in a restored 1930s modernist building near Kotzia Square, with a serious Greek-art collection and a rooftop over the old town.

items.name: The Acropolis, Parthenon, Erechtheion & Propylaea
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Acropolis of Athens
items.description: The sacred rock above the city and the reason most travellers come. Enter through the monumental Propylaea gateway to reach the Parthenon (447-432 BC), the Erechtheion with its Porch of the Caryatids, and the elegant little Temple of Athena Nike. Take a licensed private guide and go at opening or in the last two hours before close to avoid the heat and cruise crowds; the marble reflects fierce midday sun.

items.name: Temple of Athena Nike
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Acropolis of Athens
items.description: The smallest and most graceful temple on the Acropolis, perched on the bastion beside the Propylaea, built 427-424 BC to the goddess of victory. Its Ionic delicacy is a quiet counterpoint to the Parthenon's scale, and the spot gives a clean view down to the Saronic Gulf.

items.name: Odeon of Herodes Atticus
items.description: The stone Roman theatre of 161 AD tucked into the Acropolis's south slope, still used for the Athens Epidaurus Festival on summer nights. Attending a performance here, opera, orchestra or Greek tragedy under the lit Parthenon, is one of the most atmospheric evenings in the city; a concierge can arrange the best-placed seats.

items.name: The Acropolis Museum
items.description: Bernard Tschumi's glass-and-concrete museum at the foot of the rock, built over an excavated ancient neighbourhood you walk above on glass floors. The top-floor Parthenon Gallery is rotated to align with the temple itself, framing it through floor-to-ceiling glass. The restaurant terrace has a fine Acropolis view and a calm, veg-friendly menu, good for a multi-generation lunch.

items.name: Ancient Agora & Temple of Hephaestus
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Acropolis of Athens (associated monuments)
items.description: The civic heart of classical Athens, where Socrates argued and democracy took shape, spread across a green archaeological park below the Acropolis. It holds the Temple of Hephaestus, the best-preserved ancient Greek temple anywhere, and the reconstructed Stoa of Attalos, now a museum. Shaded, walkable and far less crowded than the rock above.

items.name: Roman Agora & Tower of the Winds
items.description: The Roman-era marketplace built under Caesar and Augustus, a short walk from the Ancient Agora. Its highlight is the octagonal Tower of the Winds, an ingenious 1st-century BC timepiece and weather station combining sundials, a water clock and carved wind gods, an easy, engaging stop with children.

items.name: Plaka
items.description: The oldest continuously inhabited quarter, a warren of neoclassical houses, bougainvillea and pedestrian lanes under the Acropolis. Best explored slowly on foot with a private guide who can steer you off the tourist strip to the quieter courtyards, tavernas and small churches, a gentle, multi-generation walk.

items.name: Anafiotika
items.description: A tiny pocket of whitewashed, blue-doored houses clinging to the north slope of the Acropolis, built in the 1830s by island craftsmen from Anafi who wanted a piece of home. Stepping into these silent, flowering lanes feels like being teleported to a Cycladic island in the middle of the city, a hidden gem most visitors miss.

items.name: Monastiraki & the Flea Market
items.description: The buzzing square where ancient, Byzantine and Ottoman Athens overlap, with a mosque, a library and Roman ruins in view of the Acropolis. The flea market spills through Avissinias Square and the surrounding lanes, antiques, coins, vintage and bric-a-brac, reaching full energy on Sunday mornings. A knowledgeable dealer can find genuine pieces amid the clutter.

items.name: Syntagma Square & the Changing of the Guard
items.description: The city's central square in front of the Hellenic Parliament, where the Evzones in their pleated foustanella and pom-pom shoes guard the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The guard changes on the hour; the grand ceremony with the full detachment and band is Sunday at 11am. A stately, photogenic ritual the whole family enjoys.

items.name: National Archaeological Museum
items.description: The finest collection of ancient Greek art in the world, the gold Mask of Agamemnon, the bronze Artemision Zeus/Poseidon, the intricate Antikythera Mechanism and rooms of Cycladic and classical sculpture. Vast enough to warrant a private guide who curates a focused two-hour route rather than trying to see everything.

items.name: Panathenaic (Kallimarmaro) Stadium
items.description: The only stadium in the world built entirely of marble, on the site of the ancient Panathenaic games and restored to host the first modern Olympics in 1896. You can run a lap on the track, climb to the top tier for a photo, and see original Olympic torches in the tunnel museum. An early-morning visit is best.

items.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus & Hadrian's Arch
items.description: The largest temple in ancient Greece, begun in the 6th century BC and finished by Hadrian 638 years later; fifteen colossal columns still stand against the Acropolis backdrop. Beside it, Hadrian's Arch marks the old boundary between the classical city and the Roman one, a quick, dramatic stop between Plaka and the National Garden.

items.name: Lycabettus Hill
items.description: The highest point in central Athens, crowned by a whitewashed chapel and a terrace cafe. Ride the funicular up from Kolonaki near sunset for a 360-degree sweep, the Acropolis below, the city, and the sea and islands beyond as the lights come on. Book a table on the summit for sundowners.

items.name: Filopappou Hill (Hill of the Muses)
items.description: A pine-covered hill directly across from the Acropolis, laced with landscaped stone paths by the modernist architect Dimitris Pikionis. The summit monument gives the classic postcard view of the Parthenon at eye level, the best free vantage in the city, and gloriously quiet at golden hour.

items.name: Benaki Museum of Greek Culture
items.description: A private collection in a neoclassical mansion opposite the National Garden, sweeping across Greek civilisation from prehistory through Byzantium to the War of Independence, with dazzling gold, icons and folk art. Elegant, manageable in an hour or two, with a rooftop cafe overlooking the greenery.

items.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
items.description: Home to the serene, minimalist marble figurines of the Bronze Age Cyclades that so influenced modern sculptors like Brancusi and Modigliani. A refined, beautifully lit museum with a lovely glass-roofed cafe, a natural pairing with the nearby Benaki, both in chic Kolonaki.

items.name: Byzantine and Christian Museum
items.description: One of the world's great collections of Byzantine art, icons, mosaics, frescoes, textiles and liturgical treasures, set in a garden villa on Vasilissis Sofias avenue. A quiet, uncrowded counterpoint to the classical sites, and a revelation for anyone who thinks of Greece as only ancient.

items.name: Kerameikos
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Acropolis of Athens (associated monuments)
items.description: The ancient cemetery and potters' quarter that gave us the word 'ceramic', with sculpted grave monuments lining the Street of Tombs and the old Sacred and Dipylon gates. Green, tranquil and rarely busy, a contemplative site with an excellent small on-site museum, minutes from the buzz of Gazi.

items.name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Centre (SNFCC)
items.description: Renzo Piano's landmark cultural complex, the National Library, National Opera and a vast sloping park, gifted to the city by the Niarchos Foundation. Walk up to the green roof for sea-to-Acropolis views, take in an opera, or simply let the family roam the fountains, canal and gardens. Superb contemporary architecture.

items.name: Cape Sounion & the Temple of Poseidon
items.description: A Doric temple to the sea-god on a cliff at the tip of Attica, its white columns catching the last light over the Aegean. The 70km coastal drive down the Athens Riviera is half the pleasure; time the private car to arrive for sunset, with dinner at a seafront taverna on the way back.

items.name: The Athens Riviera (Vouliagmeni & Astir)
items.description: The string of upscale coastal suburbs south of the city, Glyfada, Vouliagmeni, Kavouri, with sheltered coves, marinas and beach clubs. Astir Beach and the Four Seasons at Astir Palace are the fashionable set's playground; a half-day here balances the archaeology with sea, seafood and sun.

items.name: Lake Vouliagmeni
items.description: A rare brackish thermal lake, a flooded limestone cave ringed by cliffs, fed by underground mineral springs that hold a steady, spa-like 24°C year round. Float in the mineral water beneath the rock face, with the little doctor-fish nibbling at your feet; part of the protected Natura 2000 network.

items.name: Kolonaki Shopping
items.description: The city's most elegant quarter, climbing the slope of Lycabettus around leafy Kolonaki Square. This is where the Greek designers, international luxury houses, jewellers and galleries cluster, alongside intimate cafes for people-watching. The place for discreet, unhurried luxury shopping with a personal shopper.

items.name: Psyrri
items.description: A former workshop district turned into the city's most vibrant nightlife and dining quarter, street art, meze tavernas, cocktail dens and live rebetiko music behind unassuming doors. Atmospheric and slightly rough-edged; a private guide unlocks the best mezedopolia and the after-dark energy.

items.name: Koukaki
items.description: A leafy, residential neighbourhood on the Acropolis's southern flank, repeatedly ranked among the world's coolest districts. Its pedestrianised lanes off Dionysiou Areopagitou are lined with third-wave coffee, natural-wine bars and neighbourhood tavernas, a calm, local base a short walk from the ancient sites.

items.name: Varvakios Central Market
items.description: The thundering 19th-century covered market between Monastiraki and Omonia, the meat and fish halls, spice and olive stalls, and the herb and cheese shops of the surrounding streets. A sensory plunge into everyday Athens; go with a food guide for the freshest bites and to navigate the crowds.

items.name: Rooftop Sundowners with an Acropolis View
items.description: Athens does the illuminated-Acropolis rooftop like nowhere else, bars such as A for Athens and the terraces of Plaka and Psyrri hotels look straight at the lit rock across the tiled sea of the old town. Reserve a front-row table for dusk, when the Parthenon glows gold then floodlit against the dark.

items.name: National Garden & Zappeion
items.description: A shaded royal garden behind Parliament, palm avenues, ponds, a small menagerie and hidden ancient fragments, opening onto the elegant Zappeion hall built for the 1896 Olympics. A green, restful pause in the centre, ideal for a slow morning stroll with elders and children.

items.name: Delphi
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Archaeological Site of Delphi
items.description: The 'navel of the world', where the ancient Greeks came to consult the Oracle of Apollo, set on the dramatic slopes of Mount Parnassus above a sea of olive trees. The Sanctuary, theatre, stadium and a superb museum (the bronze Charioteer) reward a full day; roughly three hours each way, best done with a private car and guide.

items.name: Mycenae
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Archaeological Sites of Mycenae and Tiryns
items.description: The citadel of Agamemnon and heart of the Bronze Age Mycenaean world, the monumental Lion Gate, the beehive Treasury of Atreus tomb, and the shaft graves that yielded the gold funerary masks. Often combined with Nafplio and Epidaurus on a full-day Argolis loop through the Peloponnese.

items.name: Epidaurus
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Sanctuary of Asklepios at Epidaurus
items.description: The ancient healing sanctuary of Asclepius, famed for its perfectly preserved 4th-century BC theatre whose acoustics carry a whisper from the stage to the topmost of 14,000 seats. Standing at its centre to test the sound is a genuine wonder; pairs with Mycenae and Nafplio.

items.name: Nafplio
items.description: Greece's first modern capital and its most romantic small town, Venetian and neoclassical mansions, waterfront cafes, the island fortress of Bourtzi and the Palamidi castle above with its long stone stair. A graceful lunch stop on the Argolis day, or an overnight for a slower Peloponnesian escape.

items.name: Hydra
items.description: A car-free island roughly two hours by fast ferry, where stone captains' mansions rise in an amphitheatre above a perfect harbour and the only traffic is donkeys and water taxis. Long an artists' and celebrities' bolt-hole, it is chic, timeless and utterly calm, a magical day away from the mainland.

items.name: Aegina
items.description: The nearest island escape, about 40 minutes by hydrofoil from Piraeus, known for its pistachios, fishing harbour and the beautifully preserved hilltop Temple of Aphaia, part of a 'sacred triangle' with the Parthenon and Sounion. An easy, relaxed day trip when time is short.

items.name: Little Kook
items.description: A wildly over-the-top fantasy cafe on Pittaki Street that redecorates its entire lane for each season, Alice in Wonderland, Christmas, Halloween, into an immersive fairy-tale set. Kitsch to the core and a favourite with children and Instagram; a fun, whimsical stop for younger family members.

items.name: Areopagus & Pnyx Hills
items.description: Two low rock outcrops beside the Acropolis heavy with history, the Areopagus where the ancient council met and St Paul preached, and the Pnyx where the citizens' assembly invented democratic debate. Both are free, open and give lovely Acropolis and city views; the Areopagus is a popular, if slippery, sunset perch.

items.name: Panagia Kapnikarea & Byzantine Churches
items.description: The 11th-century Kapnikarea sits marooned in the middle of Ermou shopping street, a tiny domed Byzantine jewel among the fashion stores; nearby stand the Holy Apostles in the Agora and the little Metropolis. A quiet thread of medieval Athens running beneath the classical and the modern.

items.name: Piraeus & the Marinas
items.description: The great port of Athens since antiquity, its pretty Mikrolimano and Zea marina harbours ringed with seafood tavernas and yachts. Beyond the ferry bustle it has a fine Archaeological Museum and a growing dining scene; the departure point for any Saronic island run and for private-yacht charters.

items.name: Dionysiou Areopagitou Promenade
items.description: The grand pedestrian boulevard that curves around the base of the Acropolis, linking the Acropolis Museum, Herodes Atticus theatre and Thissio, marble-paved, tree-lined and closed to cars. The single loveliest walk in the city, especially in the early evening with street musicians and the rock lit above.

items.name: Theatre of Dionysus
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Acropolis of Athens (associated monuments)
items.description: The birthplace of Western theatre, carved into the Acropolis's south slope, where the tragedies of Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides were first staged. The carved marble front-row thrones for priests and dignitaries survive; included with the Acropolis ticket and easily missed on the way up.

items.name: Benaki Museum of Islamic Art
items.description: A specialist offshoot of the Benaki in a neoclassical building above Kerameikos, holding one of the world's most important collections of Islamic art, ceramics, metalwork, textiles and a reconstructed 17th-century Cairo reception room. Its rooftop cafe overlooks the ancient cemetery and the Acropolis beyond.

items.name: Meteora
items.description: Byzantine monasteries perched impossibly atop sheer sandstone pillars rising from the Thessalian plain, one of the most surreal landscapes in Greece. It is genuinely far, around four to five hours each way, so it is best as an overnight or a private-plane/train excursion rather than a same-day trip from Athens.

items.name: Wine Tasting in Attica & Nemea
items.description: Attica's old vineyards and the nearby Nemea region, Greece's most celebrated red-wine appellation, built on the indigenous Agiorgitiko grape, sit within an easy private drive of the city. A curated cellar-door day with a sommelier introduces Assyrtiko, Malagousia and Agiorgitiko away from the crowds.

items.name: Private Athens Cooking Experience
items.description: A hands-on afternoon with a Greek home cook or chef, market shopping at Varvakios, then working through mezze, dolmades, moussaka and honey-soaked sweets in a private kitchen or garden. Easily tailored for vegetarian and Jain-friendly menus, and a warm, involving activity across generations.

items.name: Delta
items.description: Athens' only two-star table, a modern-Greek tasting menu inside the Renzo Piano-designed Stavros Niarchos cultural centre, cooking that reads the whole country through one seasonal lens.

items.name: Spondi
items.description: The house that started it all, Athens' first Michelin star, awarded in 2002 and held ever since, French-rooted haute cuisine in a romantic Pangrati courtyard.

items.name: Hytra
items.description: Imaginative, Greek-ingredient tasting menus perched above the Onassis Stegi cultural centre, under young chef Yiorgos Felemegas, cerebral cooking with a rooftop bar to match.

items.name: Pelagos
items.description: Refined Greek seafood on the Riviera inside the Four Seasons Astir Palace, pristine fish and shellfish in a gardened, sea-facing setting.

items.name: CTC Urban Gastronomy
items.description: Chef Alexandros Tsiotinis' personal, ingredient-driven cooking in a low-lit Kerameikos room, one of the most creative one-star kitchens in the city.

items.name: Soil
items.description: Chef Tasos Mantis' farm-to-table kitchen fusing Greek produce with Nordic technique, a serious, sustainability-led one-star with a Green Star to prove it.

items.name: Makris Athens
items.description: A one-star newcomer set opposite the Agora ruins, where chef Petros Dimas plates Greece's regional heritage with real technique, history on the plate and out the window.

items.name: Hervé
items.description: An intimate, modern one-star in low-key Petralona, precise, personal cooking away from the tourist circuit.

items.name: The Zillers
items.description: A one-star rooftop restaurant on Mitropoleos with the cathedral and Acropolis framed above the table, under chef Pavlos Kyriakis, refined Greek cooking with the city's best backdrop.

items.name: Botrini's
items.description: Hector Botrini's long-held one-star in the northern suburbs, contemporary Mediterranean-Italian cooking from one of Greece's best-known chefs.

items.name: Tudor Hall
items.description: A one-star rooftop inside the King George, with a direct Parthenon view and elegant Greek-forward cooking, old-world glamour and a Michelin star in one.

items.name: Patio
items.description: A one-star Riviera kitchen at Vouliagmeni, plating modern Greek cooking a step from the sea.

items.name: Nolan
items.description: A Greek-Japanese bistro from chef Sotiris Kontizas, fusing his two heritages with French classics, a Bib Gourmand favourite and one of the most fun tables in the centre.

items.name: Pharaoh
items.description: Chef Manolis Papoutsakis' modern take on Greek tradition, a recent Bib Gourmand entry with generous, confident cooking.

items.name: Akra
items.description: A barbecue-inspired, laid-back Bib Gourmand kitchen doing fire and Greek produce with a relaxed hand.

items.name: Cerdo Negro 1985
items.description: A Bib Gourmand mainstay built around Iberian pork and honest, good-value cooking.

items.name: Jerár
items.description: A long-running Bib Gourmand address prized for quality-to-price, the kind of table Athenians return to.

items.name: Fine Mess Smokehouse
items.description: A Bib Gourmand smokehouse doing serious low-and-slow barbecue, relaxed, generous and very good value.

items.name: The Clumsies
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, peaked at No. 3 (2020), listed every year since 2015
items.description: The bar that put Athens on the world map, a three-storey all-day-into-late space from Kyritsis and Bakoulis, on The World's 50 Best Bars list every year since 2015, as high as No. 3 in the world.

items.name: GB Roof Garden Bar
credentials: Atop the Two-Key MICHELIN Hotel Grande Bretagne; a historic Athens rooftop institution
items.description: The rooftop of the Grande Bretagne, the grande-dame terrace for a Champagne or a Negroni with the Acropolis and Lycabettus laid out below. The classic grown-up Athens aperitivo.

items.name: Alexander's Bar
credentials: Long regarded among Europe's finest hotel bars, inside the MICHELIN Two-Key Grande Bretagne
items.description: A wood-panelled, hushed hotel bar named for its 18th-century tapestry of Alexander the Great, deep spirits, live piano, the old-world Athens nightcap.

items.name: Line
credentials: Europe's 50 Best Bars 2026, No. 1 (The Best Bar in Europe)
items.description: The city's, and now Europe's, most celebrated bar, a fermentation-led room in a former Petralona art gallery from Vasilis Kyritsis and Nikos Bakoulis, making its own wines, beers and ingredients on site.

items.name: Baba au Rum
items.description: A rum temple beloved by bartenders worldwide, an encyclopaedic rum and tiki-leaning list in a tiny, buzzy room off the old town.

items.name: A for Athens
credentials: The definitive Monastiraki-square Acropolis-view rooftop; widely listed among Athens' best rooftop bars
items.description: The rooftop everyone names first, two levels directly over Monastiraki Square with a dead-centre Acropolis view, cocktails and a young crowd at sunset.

items.name: 360 Cocktail Bar
credentials: One of the most iconic Acropolis-view rooftop bars in the historic centre
items.description: Perched above Monastiraki with one of the most photographed Acropolis panoramas in Athens, a long cocktail list and an all-day menu, reserve for the sunset seating.

items.name: Metropolis Roof Garden & M Bar
credentials: Rooftop of the MICHELIN-selected Electra Metropolis; a benchmark Athens hotel rooftop
items.description: The 10th-floor rooftop of the Electra Metropolis, a pool, Mediterranean plates and signature cocktails against a full-frame Acropolis, the most polished hotel rooftop in the centre.

plan.heading: 3 days in Athens, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: First entry to the Acropolis, up through the Propylaea to the Parthenon before the sun climbs.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Acropolis Museum, ending at the top-floor gallery framing the temple you just walked.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Spondi, the city's long-held two-star, in a courtyard in Pangrati.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Ancient Agora and the Temple of Hephaestus, then the lanes of Anafiotika above Plaka.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Benaki Museum, then coffee in the Kolonaki squares among the antique dealers.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Modern Greek tasting at Delta, inside the Stavros Niarchos centre, two stars and the harbour beyond.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A driver down the Apollo Coast to the Temple of Poseidon at Sounion, on its headland over the Aegean.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at a seaside taverna in Vouliagmeni, then the warm spring lake for a swim.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Rooftop dinner at the Hotel Grande Bretagne with the lit Acropolis in view.

items.name: Plaka & Monastiraki
items.description: The old town under the Acropolis; charming and central but touristy, best for a first stay that wants everything on foot.

items.name: Koukaki
items.description: Quiet, well-fed streets a short walk south of the Acropolis; suits those who want neighbourhood tavernas over souvenir lanes.

items.name: Pangrati
items.description: Residential and unhurried around the old stadium; for a second visit that wants to live as Athenians do.

events.name: Athens Epidaurus Festival
events.note: The city's great summer season of theatre, music and dance, staged at the Odeon of Herodes Atticus and the ancient theatre of Epidaurus.

events.name: Athens Marathon, the Authentic
events.note: The original marathon route from the plain of Marathon into the marble Panathenaic Stadium; the classic reason to visit in autumn.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Kolonaki for refinement or a rooftop in Plaka for the Acropolis at night; visit the Parthenon at opening or in the last hour before close to avoid both heat and crowds, and dress modestly if you enter any church.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Athens International (ATH); a private car covers the forty-minute run into the centre, meeting you as you clear the terminal.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver is simplest for the city and Cape Sounion; the Plaka, Monastiraki and the Acropolis slopes are walked, on marble that turns slick in rain.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Networks are quick and an eSIM (Cosmote or Vodafone) works on landing; wifi is standard in hotels and cafés.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The euro; cards are widely accepted, keep some cash for tavernas and kiosks, and leaving five to ten percent is appreciated but not expected.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: April-May and late September-October are ideal, warm, dry, the ruins comfortable to walk; July-August is fierce, dry heat (often 38C+) that makes midday Acropolis visits punishing.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Now nonstop from Delhi and Mumbai, IndiGo flies it year-round on the A321XLR (roughly 9 hours), with Aegean adding its own Delhi/Mumbai service from spring 2026. For a full business/first cabin, connect via Emirates/Etihad (Dubai/Abu Dhabi) or Turkish (Istanbul); the Gulf carriers give the strongest lounge and onward island connections.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; tap water is safe to drink. Athens is generally safe, normal caution for pickpockets around Omonia, Monastiraki and the metro. No altitude concern.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Easy, Greek cuisine is rich in vegetable, legume and grain dishes (fava, gigantes, dolmades), and Jain needs are manageable with clear instruction. Indian restaurants are present; Avocado and Nolan offer strong modern vegetarian cooking.
